title: Pioneer Zephyr, 1934
lede: The Burlington’s stainless-steel diesel train of 1934: a sloping, rounded nose and sides fluted with horizontal lines.
summary: A polished stainless-steel train with a rounded, sloping nose, a grilled dome, and horizontal fluting. Budd Company for the Burlington, 1934.

creator.name: Budd Company; exterior design by Albert Gardner Dean with Paul Philippe Cret and John Harbeson (Wikipedia)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected Daderot’s 2014 photograph of the train at the Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago, on [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pioneer_Zephyr_-_Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago)_-_DSC06911.JPG), at 1280 × 1920 px.

styles.note: A founding object of American streamlining: a rounded, sloping nose, polished metal, and horizontal fluting along the sides.

context: Built by the Budd Company in 1934 of stainless steel joined by shotwelding; exterior design by Albert Gardner Dean with the architects Paul Philippe Cret and John Harbeson. On 26 May 1934 it ran non-stop from Denver to Chicago, 1,015 miles in 13 hours 5 minutes, and appeared at the Century of Progress fair. It entered service on 11 November 1934. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Zephyr).
The train was donated to the Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago, in 1960. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Zephyr).
observed: The nose slopes back and rounds over into a dome covered by a grille of curved ribs, with a large round headlamp on top.
The cab windows form a curved band across the front.
Several thin parallel ridges run horizontally around the nose and continue along the sides as fluting.
The skirt below curves forward to a blunt, rounded lower edge.
The whole surface is polished stainless steel with visible rivet lines; the only color is a black and red “Burlington Route” sign on the nose.
interpretation: The fluting turns the speed line into structure: the parallel ridges that stiffen the steel also give the train its look. Many later graphics draw the same few parallel lines to mean stainless steel and speed.
borrow: Use a band of four to six thin parallel lines that wraps a rounded corner and continues along the edge.
Set one small saturated badge on a large field of silver-gray.

images.alt: Front three-quarter view of a polished stainless-steel train in a museum hall: a rounded, sloping nose with a ribbed grille dome and a large headlamp, a curved band of cab windows, horizontal ridges wrapping the nose, and a black and red Burlington Route sign.
images.caption: Pioneer Zephyr at the Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago. Photograph by Daderot, 2014, CC0, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pioneer_Zephyr_-_Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago)_-_DSC06911.JPG).

rights.statement: The photographer dedicated the photograph to the public domain (CC0). A train is a useful article: its shape is not protected by copyright in the United States, its country of origin. The Burlington Route sign is a trademark shown as part of the object.
